rows.title: Why do 2 Colorado towns have the same person running their chambers of commerce?
rows.standfirst: The chamber of commerce Dustin Peyser built in Timnath is so successful he was asked to run the chamber in Severance

rows.title: This western Colorado town once had sundown laws, study finds
rows.standfirst: Historians gather stories about discrimination against Black Coloradans in first state study about the legacy of slavery in the Centennial State

rows.title: Xcel’s push for fast decision on power line path is rejected by Colorado Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: Xcel tried to condemn a 550-foot strip of Cheyenne County ranchland to connect two wind farms to a substation. The landowner objected to the route.

rows.title: Are the 2 tallest buildings in Colorado Springs in foreclosure?
rows.standfirst: Yes. The two tallest buildings in Colorado Springs are set for a foreclosure auction starting Oct. 21, El Paso County records show.

rows.title: Amy Redford says Sundance connects Colorado filmmakers in an isolated industry
rows.standfirst: Redford, a director, producer and daughter of festival founder Robert Redford, sat down with The Colorado Sun ahead of an artist-led panel Tuesday at the University of Denver

rows.title: New housing development opens in Broomfield for people with disabilities, but demand far exceeds available units
rows.standfirst: Intended to serve people with intellectual, developmental disabilities, the 40-apartment Grove supportive housing complex likely will be full with in weeks

rows.title: Colorado faces a federal oil and gas leasing fire sale. One man on a Moffat County mountain is fighting back.
rows.standfirst: By the time mandatory December lease sales are finished, around 400,000 acres of land in Colorado will have been offered for exploration

rows.title: The journey from farm to table is becoming more unpredictable. It takes a flexible chef to keep local food on the menu.
rows.standfirst: Colorado restaurateurs weather the same ups and downs as their farmer friends. Being open to creating menus from what’s in the field keeps them close.

rows.title: Colorado IT office rehires 15 of 173 laid-off state workers, says overhaul will save at least $6M
rows.standfirst: The state’s Office of Information Technology also created 98 new roles, and have since hired 88 people. Meanwhile, cyber threats have increased.

rows.title: BLM ignored wildlife migration when it leased Colorado land for oil and gas drilling, lawsuit claims
rows.standfirst: Two groups want to overturn lease sales, including thousands of acres in Wyoming and northwestern Colorado that are key to elk, pronghorn and deer herds

rows.title: Judge tosses Telluride ski area owner’s lawsuit alleging coercion over failed sale
rows.standfirst: Chuck Horning claimed Telluride and Mountain Village leaders promised to end a patroller strike if he sold the ski area

rows.title: Why a world-traveling mountaineer is teaching kids to sew in a small Colorado town
rows.standfirst: A new gear-repair program in Cortez by a climber who has led Everest expeditions reduces waste in the outdoor industry and teaches kids they can put things back together

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s aerospace industry fears it may be losing ground
rows.standfirst: The state is still a leader but may not be doing enough to support industry, says new Colorado Chamber Foundation report. Plus: Downtown Denver collects more sales tax, everyone wants an apprenticeship and more!

rows.title: Colorado watching closely after federal court tosses order to keep coal power plant running in Michigan
rows.standfirst: Organizations challenging “emergency” order to keep Craig Unit 1 operable think the arguments in Michigan decision also apply here

rows.title: Colorado Broadband Office leader abruptly resigns
rows.standfirst: Brandy Reitter led the state’s effort to distribute nearly hundreds of millions in federal funds to improve broadband access

rows.title: Tax-funding squabble ends in defeat for Pueblo’s da Vinci Museum
rows.standfirst: Council appears to find work generated by the new museum isn’t “primary job creation” under new tax spending strategy

rows.title: House passes Gabe Evans’ bill aimed at addressing impact of data centers on energy costs
rows.standfirst: The legislation would require state utility regulators to consider a standard by which utilities charge data centers for the full cost of the new power and transmission upgrades needed to serve them. The bill passed by a vote of 417-3.

rows.title: Colorado Springs delays data center vote after raucous hearing
rows.standfirst: Public overwhelmingly against massive computing warehouse, as 3 protesters are arrested and 1 hit with stun gun

rows.title: AI dominated Colorado Startup Week, but the in-person experience mattered more
rows.standfirst: Artificial intelligence is impacting software development, jobs and tech startups, but a shift to the “experience economy” could be what’s next

rows.title: What’s Working: How one Colorado gardener feeds dozens in a San Luis Valley food desert
rows.standfirst: Ginny Ducale is 81, spry like Peter Pan and able to feed her town with a very green thumb. Plus: Colorado’s labor force participation rates dips to 1976 levels, Crusoe AI raises $3.9B, more!

rows.title: In a fading Colorado Eastern Plains town, one man seeks to spark new economic life with an RV park and tiny homes
rows.standfirst: It’s boom or bust out there for many Eastern Plains towns. Ben VanderWerf thinks an RV park and tiny home community will put Arriba somewhere in the happy middle.

rows.title: Meet the Denver chef who opened 3 Michelin star restaurants in 3 years
rows.standfirst: Johnny Curiel and his wife, Kasie, have opened 6 restaurants and racked up 5 Michelin nods since they opened Alma Fonda Fina in 2023

rows.title: Ski resort industry urges lawmakers to reject daylight saving legislation that would “lock the clock”
rows.standfirst: The Sunshine Protection Act would have economic and safety impacts for ski areas and mountain towns, ski resorts say

rows.title: Colorado Broadband Office rescinds more than $100M in federal awards to Maverix Broadband amid investigation
rows.standfirst: The bankrupt internet provider in Parker was paid $9M of the more than $125M in public funding awards for rural broadband service. Some work has been done, but $3.2M appears to be missing.

rows.title: Coal-burning Comanche 3 power plant back in service after a year of repairs
rows.standfirst: Shut down since August 2025, repairs to the problem-plagued plant in Pueblo could cost as much as $26 million, most covered by insurance.

rows.title: Maverix Broadband founder says a paper trail proves the company did not misuse taxpayer funds
rows.standfirst: Colorado Broadband Office allegations this week — and the cancellation of a $100M federal grant — caught the Parker-based company off guard

rows.title: Colorado Supreme Court dismisses lawsuit filed by injured snowboarder against Vail Resorts
rows.standfirst: The high court ruled that John Litterer invalidated his claims when he signed a liability waiver for a ski pass after he was injured at Breckenridge

rows.title: Cash from feds will spark $1.2B electric transmission project in eastern Colorado
rows.standfirst: Most of the cost of the 28-mile project, intended to make the electricity supply more reliable, will be passed on to customers

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver business leaders change focus to what’s best about living, working in the city
rows.standfirst: It’s a new ad campaign from business leaders who got tired of all the negativity. Plus: Denver rents 14% below pre-COVID expectations.

rows.title: Proposition 137: $175M in existing Colorado tax revenue would be routed to conservation, wildfire mitigation
rows.standfirst: Supporters say the money would shore up critical wildfire mitigation and watershed restoration as the state copes with drought, record temperatures and dramatically low snowpack

rows.title: Amendment 82: Colorado voters will decide whether to put right to natural gas in state constitution
rows.standfirst: The measure was written by conservative activists, who are offering it as a counterweight to Colorado laws and policies aimed to reduce the use of natural gas in the state as part of its goal of reducing greenhouse gases

rows.title: Colorado’s only active gold mine generated $830 million in economic activity last year, report finds
rows.standfirst: The Cripple Creek and Victor Gold Mine generates more than half of Teller County’s GDP, according to a new economic report
